decisions.question: Where does the projection live, given that D4 puts the projection and its visitor under lib/src/ir/ while TopologyPlan.definition, which must call it, is a part file of the topology library under lib/src/topology/, which the projection must import for the stage classes and visitStage?

options.label: A library lib/src/ir/projection.dart, imported back by topology.dart
options.consequence: Follows D4 to the letter and keeps the projection out of the DSL library; topology.dart and projection.dart import each other, a cycle Dart allows. Costs one import line in topology.dart.

options.label: A part file of the topology library placed under lib/src/ir/
options.consequence: No import cycle, but a part of the DSL library sitting in ir/ blurs D4's directory split and gives the projection access to the DSL's private members it does not need.

options.label: Inject the projection into TopologyPlan from outside
options.consequence: Breaks the cycle with a registration step or a function-typed global, which is mutable state in a package that must stay pure and adds an initialization order.

decisions.chosen: A library lib/src/ir/projection.dart, imported back by topology.dart
decisions.why: D4 names lib/src/ir/ for the projection and lib/src/topology/ for the definition body, and the phase Scope says the visitor is under lib/src/ir/. The dry run shows the cycle analyzes clean under the root lint set and every test and replay passes (T1.4: No issues found!, +207, topology-dsl 24 of 24, topology-ir G8 3 of 3). An analyzer or lint that reported the cycle would have changed my mind.

decisions.question: Does TopologyPlan.definition project on each read, cache its definition, or does planOf project eagerly?

options.label: A getter that projects on each read
options.consequence: No state in an @immutable plan; equal definitions each read; the rendered-alike ArgumentError surfaces at definition, not at planOf, as the routed item asks. Costs a projection per read, which live activation does once.

options.label: A late final cached field
options.consequence: One projection per plan, but a lazily assigned field in an @immutable value and an error that is cached or retried depending on Dart's late semantics.

options.label: Project inside planOf
options.consequence: planOf would throw ArgumentError for the rendered-alike corner, changing planOf's stated errors (StateError for an empty id or an unreached stage, declare's own errors).

decisions.chosen: A getter that projects on each read
decisions.why: topology-dsl@v2 states planOf's errors and has buildDefinition() return planOf(this).definition; the routed item says to let TopologyDefinition's ArgumentError propagate from definition. A getter keeps the plan inert. The package test 'G9 a plan projects again at each read of its definition ...' pins equality across reads. A contract sentence asking for one definition per plan object would have changed my mind.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md (Routed to later phases, nidana.model.11 from S132)

decisions.question: How does the visitor tell read stages, which are not edges, from the others, and how many visitor classes are there?

options.label: One class implementing StageVisitor<TransformEdge?> and SinkVisitor<TransformEdge>, read returning null
options.consequence: One 'stage and sink visitor', as the Scope says; no unreachable method; a stage adds its edge exactly when the visitor returns one.

options.label: Filter reads with an is-test before visiting, read throwing
options.consequence: An unreachable visitor method that throws, and the read test duplicated outside the visitor.

options.label: Two classes, one per visitor interface
options.consequence: Two classes sharing the edge list and the identity map.

decisions.chosen: One class implementing StageVisitor<TransformEdge?> and SinkVisitor<TransformEdge>, read returning null
decisions.why: The two interfaces share no member name, the null result encodes rule 1 directly, and the class holds the edges and the identity map both need. Function-typed members are read inside their own visitor methods, as topology-dsl@v2 requires. No evidence against; a reviewer preferring two classes would not change behavior.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topology-dsl.md (The plan: visitStage, visitSink, the note on reading function-typed members)

decisions.question: How are the phase's deliverables cut into at most 7 tasks?

options.label: Five: projection; ShellClaim; TopologyGraph with toGraph and render; the routed messages; gate and verification doc
options.consequence: Each code task has its own failing replay or tests and one reviewable seam; the graph task depends on the claim task, as G11's cases construct claims.

options.label: Four: claim and graph in one task
options.consequence: One task fewer, but a larger review and a G12 case and three G11 cases turning green in one step.

options.label: Six or seven, splitting the projection or G3 and G7 tests out
options.consequence: Tests separated from the code they pin, against the skill's right-sizing rule.

decisions.chosen: Five: projection; ShellClaim; TopologyGraph with toGraph and render; the routed messages; gate and verification doc
decisions.why: The seams match the cases: Task 1 turns 5 recording and 3 G8 cases green, Task 2 the G12 case, Task 3 the three G11 cases; the messages are independent polish a reviewer can reject alone. S139's notes proposed the same seams. The dry run ran the tasks in this order with each failing step failing and each passing step passing (T1.2 to T4.4).

decisions.question: Which of the routed items does the plan take, given the cap and one review sitting?

options.label: All ten, the four message fixes in one task of their own
options.consequence: Every routed item lands here; the message task adds about 30 library lines and one test file, reviewable alone.

options.label: Only the items the projection and graphs need
options.consequence: Leaves the grammar and naming fixes, which touch the DSL library this phase already edits, for no later phase that owns those files.

decisions.chosen: All ten, the four message fixes in one task of their own
decisions.why: nidana.model.11 is the last phase that edits the DSL library (D4: nidana.model.4, .9, .11), so the builder's message fixes have no later owner; the IR message fixes are two lines. The dry run's Task 4 is 15 edits, 4 tests, and the analyzer and every replay stay green (T4.4). decisions.question: elementsEqual takes Lists and its dartdoc names only envelopes and lineages: widen the helper, compare writes.toList(), and does this phase touch the dartdoc in lib/src/topic/, which D4 assigns to nidana.model.3 and .8?

options.label: Compare writes.toList() and rewrite the dartdoc only
options.consequence: No code change in lib/src/topic/; one comment that now names every user of the helper; a file outside this phase's declared Collides with list (both owners merged long ago).

options.label: Compare writes.toList() and leave the dartdoc
options.consequence: Stays inside D4's directories; the stale dartdoc has no later owner and stays wrong.

options.label: Widen elementsEqual to Iterable
options.consequence: A code change to a helper envelope and lineage equality use, for no gain over toList().

decisions.chosen: Compare writes.toList() and rewrite the dartdoc only
decisions.why: D4 splits directories so that phases running side by side edit disjoint files; nidana.model.11 runs alone (nidana.model.12 and .13 depend on it), so a comment edit risks no merge conflict, and no later phase owns lib/src/topic/. The routed item names the dartdoc explicitly. A reviewer who reads D4 as file ownership rather than parallelism would route the dartdoc to the end-of-node sweep instead; the code is unaffected either way.

decisions.question: How does _checkMade name a foreign handle by its position?

options.label: A names list per call: the parameter name, or inputs[i] for a list element
options.consequence: ArgumentError.name is the parameter the caller wrote (stream, events, a to d, latest, b to d) or the element (inputs[1]); ten call sites pass a const list or _elementNames('inputs', n).

options.label: One name per call and the index in the message
options.consequence: Fewer call-site changes, but combine4's fourth handle would still be named by its list position, not its parameter.

decisions.chosen: A names list per call: the parameter name, or inputs[i] for a list element
decisions.why: The finding was that a foreign fourth handle of combine4 reads 'Invalid argument (handle)'; naming the parameter as the Interface declares it (topology-dsl@v2 The builder and The handle) answers it exactly. No test or fixture pins the old name 'handle' (checked by grep; the suites assert throwsArgumentError only), and the dry run keeps topology-dsl 24 of 24 (T4.4).

decisions.question: What argument names do ShellClaim's and TopologyGraph's rejections carry, and what do the messages say? topology-ir@v1 says only 'throws ArgumentError'.

options.label: The parameter at fault: source, writes, topologies; messages without an article built from a variant name
options.consequence: Consistent with nidana.model.10's IR factories, which name the argument at fault; tests pin the names.

options.label: Unnamed ArgumentError(message)
options.consequence: Matches the contract's wording just as well but gives a caller less to go on and leaves nothing to pin.

decisions.chosen: The parameter at fault: source, writes, topologies; messages without an article built from a variant name
decisions.why: Precedent from nidana.model.10 (every IR rejection names its argument) and S132's grammar finding. Pinned by shell_claim_test.dart and topology_graph_test.dart.

decisions.question: Does a graph read each Iterable argument once? topology-ir@v1 types the arguments Iterable and states nothing about how often they are read.

options.label: Read each once, and pin it with a counting iterable
options.consequence: A lazy argument (a map over declarations, reversed, where) is evaluated once; the factory copies before it derives anything. One test.

options.label: Leave it unstated
options.consequence: An implementation that iterates twice (a length check, a second pass for topics) passes every case; a costly lazy argument would be evaluated twice.

decisions.chosen: Read each once, and pin it with a counting iterable
decisions.why: It costs nothing (sortedCopy calls toList() once and everything else derives from the copies) and it is what a caller passing a lazy view expects. The dry run's D8 (an argument read twice) passes the whole gate and fails only this test. Not a contract rule, so not a contract gap; a reviewer could drop the assertion without changing the code.

decisions.question: Which 'contracts' example topologies' does the phase Verification line mean, beyond the two the suite's G8 cases project (CheckoutFlow and every-combinator)?

options.label: Add topology-ir@v1's JSON example and two samples, transcribed from their valid/ documents
options.consequence: Package tests project the Interface's search example, the forms sample and the findings sample's quiet topology and compare with the edges the valid/ documents list; no decoder needed (nidana.model.13's).

options.label: Rely on the suite's G8 cases only
options.consequence: The other samples' projections are first compared with their documents at nidana.model.13's G19 cases.

decisions.chosen: Add topology-ir@v1's JSON example and two samples, transcribed from their valid/ documents
decisions.why: The Verification line asks for the contracts' example topologies; the JSON example is the only topology the Interface itself writes out, and forms and quiet exercise one read feeding several consumers, which the suite's G8 cases do not isolate. Transcribed by hand from hsdd/contract/fixture/topology-ir/valid/forms.json and findings.json; they pass in the dry run (C).

decisions.question: How does TopologyGraph sort claims with compareClaimKeys, which takes a record of a claim's parts, from lib/src/graph/?

options.label: A private getter ShellClaim._key returning the ClaimKey record
options.consequence: One line in ShellClaim, read by TopologyGraph in the same library; added in Task 3, where it is first used, so Task 2 has no unused element.

options.label: Build the record inline in the comparator

decisions.chosen: A private getter ShellClaim._key returning the ClaimKey record
decisions.why: Names the concept the order compares, keeps the comparator one line, and needs no public member (the Interface bullet forbids new public members). The dry run's Task 2 variant omits it and analyzes clean (T2.4).
